On Windows, MaiCord 0.5.x through 0.8.2 install this update from Settings > Updates. If you're still on 0.4.0, follow the one-time manual steps in the [0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/releases/tag/v0.5.0). On Linux, the installer and tarball installs and the AppImage update from Settings > Updates, packages through your package manager, and the musl AppImage through AppImageUpdate.

This release is mostly a cleanup: MaiCord is smaller and faster, and it fixes the faults below. Nothing you use goes away.

### What's new

- **The tray icon hides the window too.** A click on the tray icon now hides MaiCord to the tray when you're using it. When you aren't, the click brings it back, as in Telegram Desktop. A window behind other windows comes to the front. The middle click and Open still only show the window. This works on Windows and on Linux. ([#31](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/issues/31))

### Fixed in this release

- **Large servers could stay unavailable.** The first event of a server holds its channels, roles and members. When it was larger than MaiCord's read buffer, the second read used stale data and failed, so the server stayed unavailable.
- **Caption buttons.** On Linux with KDE Plasma, Minimize, Maximize and Close showed their hover near their top edge. But a press there started a window resize, and the next press was lost too. The buttons now work up to their top edge, on Linux and on Windows. On Linux, a maximized or full-screen window now shows Restore and no longer resizes from the title bar. ([#29](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/issues/29))
- **Bot profiles in voice.** The profile of a bot in a voice channel showed no tag, mutual servers or bio for about 1.5 seconds. MaiCord asked for your note first, and now it asks for the profile first. The voice card below the activity card now has the shadow edge that Discord's client paints. Thus the two cards no longer look like one card with a box under it. A later release adds Discord's hover animation of the two cards. ([#30](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/issues/30))
- **Your status on the account panel.** The avatar at the bottom left now shows your status dot, as the account menu and the member list do. Your own member list row now also follows an automatic change, such as Idle while you're away. ([#32](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/issues/32))
- **Commands of big bots.** A bot with many slash commands showed no commands on its profile card, and the command list said "Couldn't load commands". They load now.
- **Messages that didn't show.** A message that started a thread with a name longer than 128 bytes (for example many emoji or CJK characters) never appeared in the channel. Neither did a message with a thread that has no thread metadata, or a message with a mention that has no name. They all show now.
- **Thread names.** Thread names of up to 100 characters now show in full on the thread card. Before, a name over 128 bytes showed as "Thread".
- **Profile effects.** A profile effect whose layers are GIF files now shows. MaiCord read them as PNG files before.
- **Text clusters.** In Khmer, Sinhala, Myanmar or Tibetan text, a letter with decomposed marks (such as ồ after Y) now keeps its own cluster, as in HarfBuzz. Before, MaiCord joined it to the cluster of the letter before it.
- **Push-to-talk on Wayland.** Global push-to-talk only worked in the first call of each run of MaiCord. After that call, or after you changed the key or the input mode, the key worked only while the MaiCord window had the focus. It now binds again each time. Versions 0.8.0 to 0.8.2 have this problem.
- **Closed polls.** When a poll's time ran out while it was on screen, it showed "This poll has closed." in red with a Retry button, and Retry could show an error. A closed poll now shows its results only, with no vote button and no Retry.

### Faster and smaller

- MaiCord.exe is 6,326,272 bytes, 106,496 smaller than 0.8.2. The Linux program is 6,359,720 bytes, 106,728 smaller.
- No change in this release makes a measured path slower.
- **Signing in and server events.** MaiCord reads each Gateway event through the index it already built, not with new scans. READY takes 7% less time, its presences 37% less, and READY_SUPPLEMENTAL 17% less. A server's first event takes 8% less to read and 9% less to apply. Reading a voice state change takes 25% less time and a reaction 38% less. Applying an emoji update takes 30% less.
- **Messages.** Storing a new message with attachments, embeds and reactions takes about 40% less time. Reading a poll or a forwarded message from the Gateway takes 46 to 50% less.
- **Roles, emoji and the member list.** Permission and role lookups read only the roles of one server: 92% less time with 100 servers. Member list group labels take 99.7% less time and the member list sort 18% less. Each server's emoji now have their own run. With 200 servers, storing all emoji at sign-in takes 78% less time, and an emoji update 67% less.
- **Chat frames.** The unread bar no longer formats its time on every frame (ten system calls each frame before). The boxes of a frame paint 36 to 41% faster on Windows.
- **Voice.** The voice encoder (SILK) takes 13 to 15% less time for each 20 ms frame. Two more changes each take about 3 to 5% more off. Music in calls and streams decodes 11% faster, and voice playback 2 to 5% faster.
- **Video.** Reading H.264 video headers takes 36% less time, H.265 11% less and AV1 14 to 20% less. Go Live converts each captured picture up to 17% faster. On Linux, software video copies its colour planes about 10 times faster.
- **Audio on Linux.** AAC audio in videos and streams decodes 20 to 30% faster from the new transform, and 12 to 24% faster from the new Huffman decoder.
- **Pictures.** Large JPEG thumbnails decode about 3% faster.

### For developers

- The owner's rule for this release: a check stays only for an input that release code can give or that comes from outside the program. Every removed check has a trace of its release callers, and parsers and decoders have a differential fuzz against the previous code. Data from Discord, the network and files keeps its checks. Source and headers: +9,279 -17,517 lines. Tests: +4,627 -9,952 lines.
- Test-only code leaves the shipping source. This includes the notification and notification audio fixtures, because the tests link fakes now. It also includes test-only modes of the font family query and the preference writer, and counters that only tests read.
- The Gateway worker checks each event once. The UI no longer checks the mailbox records again (an owner decision). A fuzz of 1,000,007 message frames and 300,015 state frames gives the same UI state.
- JPEG, WebP/VP8, video, MP3 and AAC are now held to a PSNR floor against a reference decoder, as Opus is. SILK and the lossless formats stay bit for bit.
- Log numbers: the AAC decoder errors after `busy` move down by one. The DAVE `sender_error` values after `invalid_input` move down by two. The remote auth and CAPTCHA errors lose `invalid_input`.
- On Wayland, MaiCord ignores a window scale outside 50% to 1000% (DPI 48 to 960).
- The test build compiles each source once and shares its PCHs: about 40 CPU-seconds less for a clean Windows test build. Four tests failed under load or when another program used the clipboard: catalog service, SRW lock, AV1 stream encoder and forum media probe. They no longer depend on timing or on the machine's clipboard. The SRW lock test runs on Linux only, because on Windows it tested only Windows.
- Other builds ran on the same machine while we measured the clean test build and the test suite. Thus this note gives no figures for them. The build has 91 fewer steps. The next release measures them again on a quiet machine.
- A change of this release made the reaction synchronize step return nothing and also dropped its call from the reaction queue step. The call is back before the release, with a test, so no released version has that fault.
- AGENTS.md is shorter and adds the deflate cache rule.
